plain: To doubt someone or not trust them

webster.text: To doubt or suspect the truth, fidelity, firmness or sincerity of; not to confide in or rely on.

example.quote: He did not see the utility in this case of urging, as had been done, a particular distrust of the House of Representatives.
example.cite: James Madison, Speech in Congress on the Jay Treaty, Mar. 10, 1796
